business_problem: Blip’s legacy relational database couldn’t keep pace with its rapid growth, causing downtime and limiting flexibility.
solution_summary: Blip’s legacy relational database couldn’t keep pace with its rapid growth, causing downtime and limiting flexibility. Blip migrated its CRM module to MongoDB Atlas, gaining scalability, flexibility, and seamless Microsoft Azure integration. Blip, a fast-growing technology company, connects thousands of businesses around the world through its AI-powered communications platform. To achieve a modern, flexible, and scalable solution, Blip adopted MongoDB—and the results exceeded expectations. “Using a relational database means having a fixed schema, which does not provide the flexibility our customers need,” said Paulo Henrique Cardoso Mendonça, Director of Software Engineering at Blip. However, the decision to embrace MongoDB was “kind of a no-brainer,” as Mendonça put it. “MongoDB was in the sweet spot where we would get the flexibility and scalability we needed for the solution, all at a good price,” he said.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas Vector Search
solution_components.role: Retrieves semantically relevant context from Blip's data for AI, search, and recommendation workflows.

solution_components.name: MongoDB Atlas
solution_components.role: Provides the managed document database backing Blip's modernized application platform.

data_flow: Business documents, tickets, records, and other operational content stay in MongoDB Atlas Vector Search and MongoDB Atlas, where search indexes or vector embeddings are built and then queried in real time to supply grounded results to applications, assistants, or discovery features. Upstream and downstream integrations include AWS, Azure, CRM systems.
business_outcome: Blip eliminated downtime, improved response times by 4.5x, and laid the groundwork to scale its platform 100x.
metrics: Blip eliminated downtime, improved response times by 4.5x, and laid the groundwork to scale its platform 100x.
Average application response improved by a factor of 4.5 times—requests that previously took 40 to 50 milliseconds with SQL Server now respond in about 10 milliseconds.
Blip’s successful database migration serves as a model and proof point for its goal to scale its entire platform 100 times beyond its 2024 capacity.
architecture_clues: Vector search is part of the retrieval layer for semantic or generative-AI use cases.
